notes: Condensed from the 0.4.1 corruption-recovery work. Blast-radius reasoning and a transient-vs-permanent distinction.

messages.content: Look at the corrupt-database recovery path.
It calls unlink on graph_memory.db. That file holds every session in the storage directory, so one bad read by one session permanently deletes everyone's memory.
Three healthy sessions, one corrupt header, and the next unrelated session to connect wiped all three. The persistence_broken flag stayed False, so stats reported healthy over an empty database.
sqlite3.OperationalError subclasses DatabaseError, and OperationalError covers database is locked. Ordinary write contention was enough to trigger the delete.

Decided: quarantine by rename instead of unlink, so sqlite3 recover can salvage the file. Decided: treat lock errors as contention and destroy nothing. Completed: scoped recovery to the affected session row in persistence.py.
Added a data_loss_detected flag surfaced through stats, so destroyed memory is queryable rather than only logged.

completed_tasks: scoped recovery to the affected session row
